identity: Classical Arabic philosophical narrative prose: the cosmological-argument section of Ibn Tufayl's allegory Hayy ibn Yaqzan, in which Hayy weighs the createdness of the world (huduth al-alam) against its eternity (qidam al-alam) and derives on both horns the existence of an incorporeal Agent. Register is high MSA/classical expository-narrative: third-person past narration of an act of reasoning (fa-ra'a, wa-ra'a aydan, tabayyana lahu, fa-ntaha nazaruhu, thumma ta'ammala) wrapping long embedded syllogistic chains. Three Qur'anic quotations appear, each already isolated by the editor into its own paragraph: 262-268 (Q 67:14), 836-845 (Q 36:82), 906-921 (Q 34:3). That isolation shows the paragraphing is rhetorically sensitive, and paragraph lengths range from 7 tokens to 144, so paragraph structure is informative but not by itself sufficient.
law: A sentence ends where a syntactically complete predication is followed by a clause that is genuinely INDEPENDENT, i.e. not governed by a preceding subordinator. Positive triggers, in descending strength: (1) fa- + new perfect verb of narrative advance after a closed clause (fa-ra'a 80, fa-tabayyana 871); (2) inferential conclusion openers fa-idhan (168, 424, 762), fa-al-wajib ala dhalika (464), fa-huwa idhan (480, 679); (3) wa-qad + perfect as pluperfect/new-premise opener (447, 492); (4) adversative lakinnahu after a completed demonstration (414); (5) rhetorical question opener wa-kayfa (736); (6) a new independent nominal sentence breaking out of a closed anna-scope (wa-kull haraka 306); (7) a doxology (subhanahu 556) closing a predication. Negative triggers that FORBID a boundary even where a clause looks complete: material governed by anna/wa-anna (all objects of ra'a/tabayyana), li-anna causal clauses, law conditional chains, sawa'a concessives with their fa-innaha resumption, the disjunctive a-...am pair, the kama...fa-kadhalika correlative, PP/appositive fragments beginning mithl, and paired in-conditionals joined by wa-. Structurally: the token before every <NL> and the final token are boundaries; an <NL> never carries one. Resulting density on this document is about 24 tokens per sentence, with legitimate outliers from 7 to 87 tokens because grammar, not length, governs.
reasoning: HARD SITE 22/29/34 (paragraph 0-41). Token 15 must be read li-ma (why), not lam: lam uhdithuhu would be first person 'I did not originate it' inside a third-person report, which is incoherent, so 11-22 is an interrogative and 22 closes it. At 29 I did NOT cut: a-li-tari'in tara'a alayhi ... am li-taghayyurin hadatha fi dhatihi is ONE disjunctive question, since am al-muttasila requires the hamza in a-li-tari' and cannot open a sentence; the question therefore runs to dhatihi at 34. I also dropped a candidate at 10 (muhdith): the wa in wa-hadha al-muhdith is continuative inside one reported utterance and the terminal punctuation is the question mark at 22, so a comma reading wins. HARD SITE 80-166. Eighty-seven tokens with no available period: fa-ra'a annahu governs three coordinated wa-anna clauses, and the closing li-annahu lawi adraka ... chain of law conditionals is subordinate to the third; the first legal cut is the forced one at batil 166. HARD SITE paragraph 168-248. I read this as a chain of parallel wa-idha P fa-Q li-anna R units and cut at their unit-ends: 175 after the fa-idhan conclusion, 197 and 217 after each li-anna justification. I declined 226: wa-awwal sifat al-ajsam huwa al-imtidad (227-235) and wa-huwa munazzah an dhalika (236-248) elaborate 218-226 with al-imtidad as the antecedent of dhalika, so U4+U5+U6 read as one flowing sentence. HARD SITE 305/313. wa-kull haraka fa-la budda laha min muharrik is an independent nominal sentence, not a wa-anna coordinate, so it escapes the scope of ra'a aydan anna and forces a cut at 305; 313 then separates that universal premise from the self-contained imma/wa-imma trichotomy. HARD SITE paragraph 344-432. I declined 355 and 364 because mithl al-thiql fi al-hajar is a prepositional/appositive fragment that must attach backward, and the fa-innahu at 365 immediately unpacks that example. I declined 372 and 398 because in qusima/wa-in zida and fa-in amkana/wa-in wasala are paired conditionals joined by wa-. I cut at 382 (fa-in at 383 is inferential, moving from concrete illustration to infinite extrapolation), at 413 (lakinnahu marks the minor premise after the hypothetical), and at 423 (fa-idhan conclusion, the same marker the editor elsewhere gives a whole paragraph to). HARD SITE paragraph 434-577, the longest at 144 tokens and a clean syllogism: major premise to 446, minor premise wa-qad wajadna to 463, conclusion fa-al-wajib ala dhalika to 479, corollary fa-hiya idhan to 491, then wa-qad kana laha lahu as a pluperfect recall of his earlier physics to 528, fa-inna wujud al-alam as its consequence to 556 ending in the doxology subhanahu, and finally 557-577 which is a near-verbatim twin of 250-260, a clause the editor gave its own paragraph elsewhere and which therefore must stand as its own sentence here. HARD SITE paragraph 579-631. I placed NO internal cut despite 53 tokens: fi dhalika in wa-lam yadurruhu fi dhalika is anaphoric to the immediately preceding clause, and ala al-wajhayn jami'an in wa-sahha lahu picks up qidam al-alam aw huduthihi from the clause before it, so the wa-chain is a comma-chain reporting one outcome. HARD SITE paragraph 633-760. The wa-lamma ... wa-kanat ... tabayyana lahu construction is one 46-token sentence closing at 678, after which fa-huwa idhan opens a fresh inference. I declined 685 and 704 because sawa'a is concessive and its fa-innaha is the resumption of that concessive, not a new sentence. I cut at 735 because wa-kayfa la yakunu kadhalika is a rhetorical question and must open its own sentence. 715 is my weakest call and is marked lo: the lawla triplet is semantically welded to muta'alliqat al-wujud bihi (comma reading), but 679-735 as a single 57-token unit spans three distinct movements (causation, dependence, divine self-sufficiency), so I cut before the triplet rather than at 728. HARD SITE paragraph 847-904. Cut at 870 on the same pattern I used at 79: a closed fa-lamma...jawab followed by fa- plus a new perfect verb. I declined 889 because wa-tahaqqaqa indahu coordinates with fa-tabayyana lahu as a twin result of the same survey. Paragraphs 762-786 (fa-idhan conclusion with a wa-in concessive) and 788-834 (kama annaka ... fa-kadhalika, a correlative simile that would strand its protasis if broken) are each left whole, as are the three Qur'anic paragraphs and the closing 923-936.
